description: FalconX is a team of four passionate and innovative minds participating in the NASA Space Apps Challenge. United by our curiosity for space, technology, and science, we aim to collaborate, think creatively, and develop innovative solutions to real-world challenges using science and technology.
summary:
TrendSleuth is an advanced Earth science investigation platform engineered for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. The project directly
addresses the core hackathon mandate: enabling both students and professional scientists to explore multi-decadal satellite observations (1990–2025),
visualize regional environmental change, and test whether observed trajectories constitute statistically significant climatic trends rather than random
historical fluctuations.
Built on Next.js 16 and styled with modern responsive components, TrendSleuth pioneers a Dual-Persona Architecture. In ■ Student Mode, complex
climate science is translated into intuitive investigative clues, interactive 3D WebGL globe navigation, colorful Ed Hawkins barcode warming stripes, and
plain-English agricultural advisories. In ■ Expert Mode, the platform unlocks an uncompromising scientific laboratory executing full non-parametric
statistical engines: the Mann-Kendall Rank Trend Test (S, Z, p-value), the Hamed-Rao Variance Correction for serial autocorrelation, and the
Theil-Sen Robust Median Estimator with exact 95% confidence intervals.
By ingesting 432 consecutive monthly observations per variable across six core Earth system indicators (Surface Temperature, Precipitation, Solar
Insolation, Root-Zone Soil Moisture, Wind Speed, and Relative Humidity) from NASA POWER, MERRA-2, and GLDAS, TrendSleuth bridges the gap
between raw Earth observation telemetry and actionable climate intelligence.
details:
PROJECT DETAILS & DUAL-MODE ARCHITECTURE

A central requirement of the NASA Space Apps Challenge was designing for diverse user personas — high school and college students alongside research scientists and experienced analysts. TrendSleuth solves this through a unified dynamic reactive state that instantly adapts visual depth, tone, terminology, and mathematical transparency without sacrificing scientific rigor.

Empirical Real-World Regional Case Studies:

• Arctic Polar Thaw (Svalbard, Norway): Demonstrates Arctic Amplification with accelerated warming of +1.18 °C/decade, strongly significant (p < 0.001) with drying root-zone moisture anomalies.

• Sonoran Desert Heat Strain (Phoenix, USA): Persistent escalating summer heat (+0.54 °C/decade) coupled with decreasing relative humidity, driving extreme HVAC grid cooling surges.

• Tropical Monsoon Coast (Kochi, India): Elevated coastal thermal baseline (+0.24 °C/decade) accompanied by high interannual precipitation volatility during June–September monsoon periods.

• Amazon Rainforest Hydrology (Manaus, Brazil): Multi-decadal soil moisture depletion and extended dry spells, highlighting vulnerability to basin-wide drought cycles.

• Arabian Gulf Thermal Surge (Dubai & Abu Dhabi, UAE): Hyper-arid thermal acceleration (+0.35 °C/decade) with stable, minimal precipitation (< 0.2 mm/day) and intense solar insolation.

MATHEMATICAL & CLIMATOLOGICAL FRAMEWORK

Earth science observations violate classical assumptions of ordinary least squares (OLS) regression: environmental records exhibit significant seasonality, skewness, outliers, and serial autocorrelation. TrendSleuth implements a mathematically sound, peer-reviewed non-parametric statistical suite:

1. Deseasonalization (Monthly Anomaly Transform):

To eliminate the annual solar cycle without losing temporal resolution, monthly climatological baselines are computed: µ_m = (1/N) ∑ x_{y,m}. The deseasonalized anomaly time series is evaluated as: x'_{y,m} = x_{y,m} - µ_m.

2. Mann-Kendall Non-Parametric Rank Trend Test:

Evaluates monotonic upward or downward trend without assuming normality. The test statistic ‘S’ is defined as:

S = ∑_{k=1}^{n-1} ∑_{j=k+1}^n sgn(x_j - x_k)

where sgn(θ) = +1 if θ > 0, 0 if θ = 0, -1 if θ < 0.

Variance with tie correction for tied observation groups t_i:

Var(S) = (1/18) [ n(n - 1)(2n + 5) - ∑_{i=1}^m t_i(t_i - 1)(2t_i + 5) ]

3. Hamed-Rao Modified Variance for Serial Autocorrelation:

Positive serial autocorrelation (memory between consecutive months) inflates false-positive trend significance. TrendSleuth corrects the variance using the empirical lag-k autocorrelation factor η (Hamed & Rao, 1998):

η = 1 + [ 2 / (n(n - 1)(n - 2)) ] ∑_{k=1}^{n-1} (n - k)(n - k - 1)(n - k - 2) r_k^*

Var*(S) = Var(S) × η

The standardized test statistic Z_{MK} is computed and evaluated against standard normal two-sided critical values (p < 0.05).

4. Theil-Sen Robust Median Slope Estimator:

The true rate of change (velocity per year/decade) is computed as the median of all pairwise coordinate slopes:

β = median( (x_j - x_k) / (j - k) ) ∀ 1 ≤ k < j ≤ n

Theil-Sen provides a 29% breakdown point, remaining immune to catastrophic weather outliers, volcanic spikes, or sensor glitches.

5. Exact 95% Non-Parametric Confidence Intervals:

Confidence limits are derived from the ranked pairwise slope distribution using the standard normal critical value C_α = Z_{1-α/2} √(Var*(S)), yielding rigorous lower and upper velocity boundaries: [Sen_lo, Sen_hi].
